files.Title: AFPS.ADS
files.Summary: FireWeaponBase-derived ADS handler: Fire() records aim intent and a per-frame reconcile blends the aim-down-sights state (pos/rot/FOV/spread plus crosshair/scope UI). Always CanFireNow=false (no recoil kick).

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ADSPose
files.Summary: Shared ADS pose math. The runtime pipeline ( / ) and the editor ADS preview both evaluate the aimed pose through here, so what a designer previews in the editor can't drift from what the player actually sees.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_AI
files.Summary: Demo NavMesh AI: each Update steers NavMeshAgent toward the closest enemy agent.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_AbilityPickup
files.Summary:
Pickup interactable that equips an ability into AFPS_AbilitySystem the same way AFPS_WeaponObject equips a weapon into AFPS_WeaponSystem.

Equip flow (mirrors AFPS_WeaponObject): Interact / collider pickup → calls inventory.FindGridForItem with requireExplicitCategory=true. If a single-slot grid matches, AddItemToGrid runs and we wire onPlacedInEquipmentSlot / onRemovedFromEquipmentSlot on the resulting AFPS_ItemObject. AddItemToGrid does not fire onPlacedInEquipmentSlot, so we explicitly call for the slot the grid maps to.

Later drags between equipment slots and the stash run through the wired listeners (drag-out → unequip; drag-in → equip). The slot index is looked up from , so any drag into a non-ability slot (e.g. the player rearranging into a generic stash grid) leaves AbilitySystem untouched.

Drop: reactivates the world GameObject, destroys the inventory ItemObject, unequips the ability instance from AbilitySystem, throws via rigidbody. Listener is unwired first so the teardown-side onRemovedFromEquipmentSlot doesn't re-enter the handler.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_AbilitySystem
files.Summary:
Ability system. Holds up to slots (mapped to the AbilityOne/Two/Three inputs). Two equip paths coexist:

  1. Inspector loadout — designer fills with AbilityHolder entries whose ability field points at a scene-attached AbilityBase. Those abilities are equipped from the start and are not destroyed on any unequip path.
  2. Pickup — AFPS_AbilityPickup calls with a prefab. The system instantiates a copy as a child, builds a runtime holder copying trigger defaults from the prefab, and the unequip path destroys the instance. Extend by inheriting AbilityBase and overriding ActivateAbility(bool pressed = true). Examples: Scripts/Abilities/Dash.cs, GrapplingHook.cs.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Agent
files.Summary: Identity component for any scene actor (player or AI): stores team affiliation and exposes team/ally query helpers used by .

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_AgentManager
files.Summary: Singleton manager that registers all scene instances at startup and exposes spatial queries for closest agent by team, ally, and enemy relationships.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_AmmoStateToggle.CountSource
files.Summary: Which value drives the toggle evaluation.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_AmmoStateToggle.ToggleEntry
files.Summary: One target GameObject and the inclusive count range over which it is enabled.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_AmmoStateToggle
files.Summary:
Decoupled, count-driven GameObject toggler for a weapon. Conceptually the world-space sibling of 's sprite-by-count system: instead of swapping a sprite asset on an inventory icon, it enables/disables child GameObjects on the weapon model based on a live count. The count comes either from (CurrentMag / Reserve / sum) or straight from the weapon item's stored contents — summed stack sizes (StoredStackSum) or the number of distinct stored entries (StoredItemCount), mirroring .

Semantics are cumulative ranges — every entry whose [minCount, maxCount] range contains the current count is enabled simultaneously (e.g. one visible shell GameObject per loaded round, or a low-ammo warning light active only while the count is between two bounds). Pure SetActive toggling; no sprite assignment.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_AnimationEventEntry
files.Summary: One keyed cosmetic response to an animation event: an optional one-shot sound plus an optional UnityEvent for anything else (particles, prop toggles, socket spawns).

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ArmAnimationSettings
files.Summary: Maps each MovementState to an ArmAnimation; consumed by AFPS_ArmsController to drive the arm Animator per state.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ArmsAnimSlot
files.Summary: Clip slots the arms animator template exposes. Enum order IS the index order used by every per-slot array in , so the tables stay aligned without a dictionary lookup. Append new slots at the END only.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ArmsAnimatorContract
files.Summary:
Single source of truth for the shared movement arms' animator: state names, parameter names, and their pre-hashed IDs. The arms mirror deliberately — same two-layer shape, same locomotion vocabulary, same swim directions — so that learning one teaches you the other, and so the two can be driven from one shared movement snapshot.

Every hash is a static readonly computed from a const string: a pure computation with no mutable static state, so it survives Enter Play Mode with domain reload disabled.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ArmsController
files.Summary:
Drives the shared first-person movement arms — the rig used for climbing, ledge hangs, mantles, slides and swimming, independent of whichever weapon is held.

Rebuilt on the same architecture as : one generated template controller, a per-player AnimatorOverrideController whose named slots you drop clips into, hashed state and parameter IDs from , and playback driven by Play/CrossFade rather than triggers. Continuous poses are POLLED from the shared snapshot — the same one the weapon animator reads, so the arms and the weapon can never disagree about what the player is doing. Only genuine one-shots (grab, mantle, slide-start) are pushed in by callers.

LEGACY MODE: when the assigned controller is not contract-shaped — most importantly the shipped hand-authored Arms.controller — this component behaves exactly as it always has, string parameters and triggers included. Existing projects therefore upgrade with no change in behaviour and migrate when they choose to, with the Set Up Arms Animations button on this component.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_AudioManager
files.Summary: Static helper for playing a random clip from a RandomAudioClipContainer at a random volume via PlayOneShot.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Camera
files.Summary: First-person camera controller: processes look input, applies FOV scaling, headbob (sine or curve), hit-bob physics, wallrun/slide/movement tilt, ledge-hang yaw clamping, and vignette post-processing each LateUpdate.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Checkpoint
files.Summary: Trigger checkpoint that snapshots player HP and active status effects on first contact; restores from the frozen state on death.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_CheckpointManager
files.Summary: Persistent singleton that tracks the last activated and restores player position, HP, and status effects on death.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_CheckpointRespawnStrategy
files.Summary: Respawns through the existing — same position, same frozen HP, same frozen status effects as the asset's original death behaviour. This is the strategy that keeps a project's feel unchanged when it adopts the death screen.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ClimbMovementSettings
files.Summary: Wall-climb preset: detection radius/layers, PID-driven climb velocity curve, stamina drain, disconnect impulse, horizontal movement multiplier, and per-wall climb-count cap.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ColdEfect
files.Summary: Cold status side effect stub; override to implement slow/freeze logic.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Compass
files.Summary: Drives the HUD compass: samples camera yaw each frame and pushes heading to UIManager which fans out to the active . Renderer-agnostic — UGUI and UI Toolkit HUDs share the same heading feed.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ContainerInventory
files.Summary:
A lootable world container — chest, crate, locker, dead body, wall stash. Interacting binds its contents to the inventory's secondary grid, resized to the size declared here, so the player loots through the same drag / rotate / stack interactions they already use on their own inventory.

Contents are live instances. While closed they are deactivated and parked under this GameObject, keeping their stack sizes, rotation, nested storage and the world object they were picked up from; opening re-seats them in the cells they were left in. Authored loot (, ) stays as lightweight descriptors until first open.

Setup: put this on a world object with a collider on the interaction layer, and give the player an .

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ContainerLootTable.LootEntry
files.Summary: One candidate line in a loot table: what can drop, how likely, and how big a stack.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ContainerLootTable
files.Summary:
Weighted loot table for . Rolls a list of entries — the same serialisable shape the rest of the inventory uses for nested storage — so the result can sit dormant on a closed container and be materialised into real item objects the first time it is opened.

Two passes run per roll: guaranteed entries always attempt (gated only by their own chance), then weighted entries fill the remaining roll count, picked proportionally to weight.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ContainerUIController
files.Summary:
Player-side owner of the secondary ("container") inventory panel. One pooled is re-sized and re-pointed for whichever the player has open, so a 3x2 ammo box and a 10x6 corpse share the same grid, binding and UI element.

It binds and unbinds containers (one at a time), marks the grid external so the rest of the inventory treats its contents as not-yet-owned loot, drives the UXML panel (title, live weight, Close and Take All), and closes the container when the inventory closes, the player walks away, or the player dies.

Place it on the same GameObject as (or anywhere in the player hierarchy) and point it at the secondary grid. The UXML fields are optional: with no UIDocument assigned it still binds containers and simply shows/hides the grid GameObject, which is what a UGUI-based setup wants.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ControlAxes
files.Summary: Which player-control channels a lock suppresses. Flags, so a lock can hold any combination.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ControlLockStatusBehaviour
files.Summary:
Status behaviour that locks the player's controls for the effect's duration — a Stun (lock everything), a Root/Snare (movement only), a Silence-style disarm (firing only), or any mix. Holds a reference-counted lock on while active and releases it when the effect ends, so overlapping locks compose correctly.

Player-only: it drives the player's movement/camera/weapon systems, so it no-ops on AI (whose "stun" would be an AI-side concern). The control lock is reference-counted, so stacking two stuns and having one expire keeps the player locked until the second ends.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_CorpseContainer
files.Summary:
Turns a dead entity into a lootable body. Watches an and, the moment it dies, fills the on this GameObject with the entity's gear — a death loot table, an authored carried-items list, and optionally its equipped weapons — then enables the container so the player can interact with it.

While alive the container component is disabled, which is the interaction system's off-switch: no interaction box, no prompt, no Interact() call. A living enemy therefore shows no loot affordance without any extra wiring.

For NPCs only. On the player it refuses to run and points you at , which answers the same question without riding along through respawn as a lootable body attached to the living player.

Setup: put this and on the entity (or on a child owning the corpse collider), leave the references empty to auto-resolve, and give the container a verb like "Loot". The collider the player looks at must be on the same GameObject as the container — the interaction system reads the collider it hits, and does not walk up to parents.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_CrosshairSettings
files.Summary: Maps MovementState → Crosshair; UIManager selects the active entry each frame and transitions via IHUDLayer.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_CrouchAndSlideSettings
files.Summary: Crouch and slide preset: speed thresholds, collider height, movement force/drag, slide impulse, and ceiling-clearance check distance.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_DamageNumberManager
files.Summary: Spawns world-space floating damage/heal numbers in response to . Only renders hits dealt by the local player (instigator with an flagged isPlayer). Numbers are pooled objects built procedurally (no prefab), billboarded to , animated via the curves on . Rapid hits on the same target inside the accumulation window merge into one growing number.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_DamageNumberSettings
files.Summary: Preset driving : world-space floating damage/heal numbers — text style, crit and heal colouring, rise/fade animation, and same-target accumulation. One asset can be shared by every weapon's hit feedback.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_DamageType
files.Summary: ScriptableObject identity for a kind of damage (Ballistic, Fire, Poison, …). Replaces the old DamageType enum so new types can be authored as assets and carry data: a display name and colour for UI, a death-screen noun, and an optional list of status effects to auto-apply on a direct hit. Referenced by , , weapon/explosion settings, and .

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_DashSettings
files.Summary:
Dash preset: every tuning value for — direction mode and force, the pre-dash velocity reset, the momentum the dash keeps afterwards, and the optional charge-up windup.

Swap the asset to swap the whole feel of the dash. Only the SFX containers stay on the component, since those are per-instance rather than per-preset.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_DeathBodyHandler
files.Summary:
Optional companion to that decides what the camera is looking at during a death. A freezecam or orbit shot pointed at a hidden first-person capsule looks broken — this is what gives those modes a subject.

Add it to the player only when the death screen actually leaves first person; the controller works fine without it. Whatever this produces is written back into , which is the transform every camera mode frames.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_DeathCameraMode
files.Summary:
Base class for everything the camera can do while the player is dead. Subclass, override , and the asset gets a new death camera with no changes to the death controller — the same extension model as .

Subclasses only describe where the camera wants to be; the blend from the pose the player died holding into that target is handled here so every mode gets easing, dolly-in, and FOV blending for free.

Runtime state: modes are shared assets, so any per-death state a subclass caches must be reset in . The shipped modes are pure functions of elapsed time and the context.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_DeathController
files.Summary:
Owns the window between dying and respawning. Add it to the player and stops respawning instantly and hands the death over here instead; remove it and the asset reverts to its original instant-checkpoint behaviour. Nothing else has to change either way — the presence of this component is the switch.

The sequence itself is described entirely by the asset in : timing, camera mode, respawn strategy, screen text, and policy. Swapping that one asset is how a flat "YOU DIED" overlay becomes a killcam.

Runs at a late execution order so its camera drive lands after has had its turn, and times everything on the unscaled clock so death-screen countdowns survive time dilation.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_DeathScreenUGUI
files.Summary:
UGUI death screen, for projects still on the Canvas-based HUD. Functionally identical to — same contract, same settings, same behaviour — so the two can be swapped on the controller without touching anything else.

Every reference is optional: wire up only the pieces the screen actually shows.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_DeathScreenUIToolkit
files.Summary:
UI Toolkit death screen, rendered from UI Toolkit/DeathScreen/DeathScreen.uxml. Matches how the pause and main menus are built in this asset: a on its own GameObject, elements resolved by name, styling left entirely to USS.

Every element is optional — delete the countdown label or the prompt from the UXML and this keeps working. Only the names matter, so a project can rebuild the layout from scratch as long as it keeps them.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_DeathScreenView
files.Summary:
Base for whatever draws the death screen. talks to this and nothing else, so the UGUI and UI Toolkit implementations are interchangeable — and a project can subclass this to render the screen its own way without touching the death flow.

Leaving the controller's view slot empty is a supported configuration: the death sequence still runs its camera, timing, and respawn, it just draws no UI. That is how a purely cinematic death (freezecam into an automatic respawn) is authored.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_DeathSettings
files.Summary:
One death screen, described end to end: how long the sequence runs, what the camera does, what happens to the body, what the screen says, and what brings the player back.

Swapping this one asset on is the whole customisation story — the shipped presets in Presets/Death are the same component configured four different ways.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_DragableObject
files.Summary: Physics-driven holdable object: PID controllers drive position and optionally rotation toward a camera-relative hold point each FixedUpdate; auto-releases when distance exceeds disconnectDistance.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_EquipAnimationWeaponObjectSettings
files.Summary: Weapon equip/de-equip animation preset: resting position/rotation, equip start/end transforms, and per-axis LeanTween duration and easing.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_EventRespawnStrategy
files.Summary:
Does nothing itself — raises and lets your own code decide where the player goes. This is the escape hatch for anything the shipped strategies don't cover: a networked spawn handshake, a spectator queue, a wave-based arena that spawns you when the round flips.

Subscribe before the player can die (Awake/OnEnable on a manager), move the player in the handler, and set to match whether your handler also sets HP.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Explosion
files.Summary: OverlapSphere explosion: LOS wall-check per collider, falloff-curve damage, self-damage/force toggles, and an optional self-destruct timer.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ExplosionMovementSettings
files.Summary: Explosion response preset: toggles input-disable and drag-override on blast hit, with per-explosion duration controlled by the caller.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_FOVEffectsCameraSettings
files.Summary: Velocity-driven FOV preset for main and weapon cameras. The peak velocity FOV is a multiplier of the (runtime-mutable) base FOV, reached as the player approaches their configured top movement speed — so the effect scales with both the player's chosen FOV and their movement tuning, with no manual velocity threshold to keep in sync.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Fluid
files.Summary: Trigger volume that writes fluid state into AFPS_Movement on enter/exit and applies linearDamping to non-player rigidbodies.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_FluidMovementSettings
files.Summary: Fluid (swim/water) preset: movement mode (Default/Swim/NoSwim), swim speed, acceleration, and ascend/descend rates.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_FollowBodyDeathCamera
files.Summary: Third-person camera that tracks the body — the corpse prefab or ragdoll produced by , or the player transform when neither exists. Pairs with a ragdoll: the camera hangs back at a fixed offset while the body tumbles, so the fall is readable.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_FootstepSettings
files.Summary: ScriptableObject map from PhysicsMaterial → AudioResource for surface-driven footstep sounds; defaultAudioResource plays on unmapped surfaces.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_FreezeDeathCamera
files.Summary:
Holds the exact camera pose the player died with — the classic freezecam. The camera stops being driven by the body, so it no longer bobs, tilts, or follows a ragdoll falling over: the last frame of gameplay simply hangs there.

The optional dolly and drift turn that frozen frame into a slow reveal without leaving the pose: pull back to show the room the player died in, rise to look down at the body, or add a barely perceptible yaw so the shot doesn't read as a screenshot.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_GrapplingHookSettings
files.Summary:
Grappling hook preset: every tuning value for — attach rules, reel and momentum, pendulum tension, swing control, movable-anchor mass split, and the auto-detach conditions.

Swap the asset to swap the whole feel of the grapple. Scene-bound references (the rope LineRenderer) and the SFX containers stay on the component, since those are per-instance rather than per-preset.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_GroundingAndSlopeMovementSettings
files.Summary: Grounding and slope preset: sphere-cast radius/distance/layers, slope max-angle and push force, and PID-driven float/step-height controller tuning.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_HeadbobCameraSettings
files.Summary: Procedural headbob preset: Sine or Curve mode, velocity-scaled frequency/amplitude, per-state suppression, and stabilization tuning.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Health
files.Summary: Core HP component: manages base HP and overheal pools, per-type damage resistances, status effect lifecycle, death/respawn flow via , and drives health HUD.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_HealthAffectArea
files.Summary: Trigger volume that applies a signed HP delta to any occupant on an independent per-target timer, routing negative deltas through (typed) and positive through .

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_HealthBar
files.Summary: World-space health bar for the on this object (or a parent). Builds a billboarded UGUI bar (background + left-anchored fill) procedurally — no prefab or material to wire. The fill tracks base HP (overheal excluded) and recolors by the discrete thresholds on . Add this to any entity that should show a bar; the player typically uses the screen HUD instead.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_HealthBarSettings
files.Summary: Shared preset for : bar dimensions, placement, background, and discrete per-threshold fill colors. One asset can drive every entity's bar.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_HitBobCameraSettings
files.Summary: Acceleration-driven camera bob preset: acceleration scale/clamp, rebound, damping, and per-axis rotation multipliers for physics-impact shake.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Hitbox
files.Summary: Per-collider damage relay for body-part criticals. Sits on a child collider of a character (head, torso, limb), scales incoming damage by , can optionally bypass the owner's per-type resistance and the firing weapon's range falloff, tags the hit with for crit styling, then forwards the result to the owning . Implements so weapons can apply damage to the exact collider they hit without knowing whether it is a hitbox or the body itself. Radius damage () targets directly and therefore never receives this multiplier.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Hitmarker
files.Summary: UGUI hitmarker instance: runs start→base→end LeanTween sequence driven by AFPS_HitmarkerSettings, then self-destructs.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_HitmarkerSettings
files.Summary: Three-phase hitmarker preset (start→base hold→end): sprite, sound + delay, per-phase size/rotation/color and LeanTween easing.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_HorizontalMovementSettings
files.Summary: Ground and air movement preset: drag, acceleration, max speed, and air-strafe speed for both grounded and airborne states.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_InputManager
files.Summary: Bootstraps the static AFPS_PlayerActions instance, applies saved keybindings, enables the Player action map, and exposes ToggleActionMap for UI/gameplay context switches.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Interactable
files.Summary:
Base for anything the player can target and interact with. Holds only look-and-interact concerns: the UI label, the held-press timer, and the Interact/EndInteract verbs. Inventory pickup lives on AFPS_PickupInteractable.

Off-switch API: set interactable.enabled = false to make AFPS_InteractionSystem ignore this object entirely — no interaction box, no name/description UI, no Interact() callbacks. Useful while a dying object plays its death/explosion effect on a delay before Destroy(). Disable also stops the host MonoBehaviour's Update/FixedUpdate (relevant for subclasses like AFPS_DragableObject which run physics per-frame).

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_InteractionCollider
files.Summary: Trigger collider that auto-picks up objects with PickupType.OnTouch on overlap; non-pickup interactables are ignored and must be reached via the spherecast path in .

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_InteractionSystem
files.Summary: Player interaction controller: runs dual spherecasts each Update (weapon and general layers), manages look-targeting UI, routes press/held-press events to or , and owns the active reference.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_InventoryDeathHandler
files.Summary:
Decides what happens to the player's inventory when they die: keep it, drop it into a lootable container at the death position, or destroy it.

Hooks , which fires before either respawn path runs, so the death position is still the player's real one. Nothing else in the death system touches the inventory, so this component is the whole feature — remove it and deaths keep everything.

Dropped items keep their identity: stack sizes, rotation, nested storage, and the world objects they were picked up from all survive into the container, so looting your own grave returns exactly what you lost.

Drop To Container can put the loot in its own container on the ground, or inside the corpse the death sequence spawns so the body itself is the stash — see . This is the player's body-loot component; is the NPC equivalent and refuses to run alongside it.

Setup: put it on the player next to , leave the references empty to auto-resolve, and pick a policy. Drop To Container additionally needs a prefab carrying an .

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_InventoryGrid
files.Summary: A single inventory grid panel: allocates a cell array, enforces category/size constraints, exposes weight and capacity queries, and sets on pointer entry.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_InventoryGridUIBinding
files.Summary: Per-grid UI Toolkit renderer. Coexists with UGUI renderer (hidden via CanvasGroup). Owns cellPixelSize (panel-space). On first layout: sets baseRes=Screen.size (disables system's adjustedCellSize scaling) and cellSize=cellPixelSize*panelScale (on-screen px). Multiple bindings cooperate — keep cellPixelSize uniform (last-write-wins otherwise).

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_InventorySystem
files.Summary: Grid-based inventory system: manages item placement, stacking, rotation, swapping, drag-hold, right-click menus, and double-click consolidation across multiple instances.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_InventoryUIRenderer
files.Summary:
Top-level UI Toolkit renderer. Hides the original UGUI inventory canvas and draws a "held item" mirror VisualElement that follows the mouse, mirroring inventorySystem.currentItem each frame (sprite, size, rotation).

Pair with one AFPS_InventoryGridUIBinding per AFPS_InventoryGrid. All coordinate conversions go through the binding's PanelPerScreen helper so the renderer is robust to PanelSettings scale-mode changes.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_InventoryWeightDisplay.PanelWeightGroup
files.Summary: Binds a named UXML Label to one or more grids whose weights are summed and formatted into it each frame.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_InventoryWeightDisplay
files.Summary: Binds UI Toolkit weight labels to live AFPS_InventoryGrid weights. Per-group: each PanelWeightGroup sums its grids into one Label. Top-bar: optional aggregate label. Uses GetGridWeight (includes nested storage via GetTotalWeight).

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Item
files.Summary: Item definition: grid size, stack, weight, category, storage container settings, count-driven sprite/HUD icon swaps, and context menu reference.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ItemCategory
files.Summary: Tag SO used by grids and items to enforce category-based placement restrictions.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ItemInteractable
files.Summary: Plain (non-weapon) pickup interactable. Interact: base.Pickup → add to inventory, reparent + disable GO. Refused if no grid fits (no input consumed). Drop: base.Drop reactivates GO, then positions in front of camera and launches with dropForce + dropTorque. Use AFPS_WeaponObject for equip-on-pickup weapon behavior.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ItemMenu
files.Summary: List of button prefabs spawned as the right-click context menu for an inventory item.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ItemMenuController
files.Summary: UGUI IItemMenuRenderer. Wraps CreateItemMenu/DestroyCurrentItemMenu so InventorySystem dispatches uniformly across UGUI and UI Toolkit.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ItemMenuUIToolkit
files.Summary: UI Toolkit IItemMenuRenderer. Spawns a floating VisualElement menu with one Button per AFPS_ItemMenu entry. Per-button logic is delegated: each prefab (UGUI ItemMenuButtonBase) is instantiated off-screen, SetItem+OnPress, then destroyed — Consume/Drop/Use/etc. work unchanged. Self-registers as activeItemMenu in Initialize, overriding the UGUI controller. Mirrors IHUDLayer pattern.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ItemObject
files.Summary: Runtime UI representation of an inventory item: manages grid position, rotation, stack count, sprite display, storage sub-items, and equipment-slot event callbacks.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_KeepFirstPersonDeathCamera
files.Summary: Leaves the camera exactly where it is — the player keeps their own first-person view, and can keep looking around, while the death screen sits on top. This is the mode behind a flat "YOU DIED" overlay with a respawn button.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_KillInfo
files.Summary:
A resolved "who killed whom" record, built by whenever ANY entity dies — player, AI, or a destructible prop — and delivered through the health's event and the static event. Both are empty hooks by default: subscribe to drive a killfeed, scoring, on-death loot, AI aggro, achievements, and so on, without touching the health system itself.

It reads the victim's latched , so status-effect deaths attribute correctly (a death from your rocket's Burn credits you), matching the floating-number and death-screen attribution.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_KillerDeathCamera
files.Summary:
Killcam: frames whoever landed the killing blow, resolved from the latched instigator. The camera sits over the victim's body and looks down the line to the killer, keeping them framed as they move.

Deaths with nothing to blame — a fall, drowning, a status effect that outlived its caster — have no killer to point at. Set so those still play something deliberate instead of holding a shot of empty air.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_KnockbackStatusBehaviour
files.Summary:
Status behaviour that knocks the player back and strips their control until they land again — the classic "launched and helpless" effect. On apply it launches the player's Rigidbody away from whoever applied the effect (plus an upward kick) and holds a control lock that releases itself the moment the player touches the ground; the effect's own duration is a safety cap that also releases the lock if the player somehow never lands.

Player-only (drives the player's Rigidbody + control lock). Direction comes from the effect's instigator () — so a rocket, a punch, or a barrel blast all shove the player away from the source.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Ladder
files.Summary: Climbable ladder surface: sets AFPS_Movement.currentLadder via trigger overlap or explicit Interact depending on useInteractionSystem.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_LadderMovementSettings

files.Summary:
Builds an from an .

This exists so the swim and locomotion rules live in exactly one place. They were duplicated the moment a second animation system needed them, and duplicated rules drift: the arms and the weapon disagreeing about whether the player is swimming is a bug nobody would think to look for.

Pure and allocation-free — safe to call every frame, and safe under Enter Play Mode with domain reload disabled (no static state of any kind).

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_MovementAnimationSnapshot
files.Summary:
One frame's answer to "what is the player doing?", in the form every animation system in the asset needs it. Sampled once per consumer per frame and passed around by value.

Every field is derived, never authored: the weapon and arms animators must agree on what counts as swimming or climbing, and the only way to guarantee that is for neither of them to decide.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_MovementEffectsCameraSettings

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_OrbitDeathCamera
files.Summary: Slowly circles the body — the cinematic death shot. Radius and height can widen over the orbit, so the camera both pulls away from and rises above the death as it goes around, which is what sells a long "hold until the player presses respawn" screen.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_PickupInteractable

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_PlayerControlLock
files.Summary:
Reference-counted control lock on the player. Status effects (Stun, Knockback) — or any other system — hold a lock over one or more ; the player regains a channel only when the LAST holder suppressing it releases, so overlapping locks never fight. Also supports "lock until the player lands again" for knockback.

Added automatically to the player the first time a lock is requested (like the status VFX registry) — you never place it by hand. It drives , , and , saving and restoring the look/firing flags so releasing a lock can't stomp a menu that independently disabled them.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_PlayerSoundManager
files.Summary: Routes movement events (jump, air-jump, land, sprint, slide, footsteps) to AudioSources; footstep interval scales inversely with speed.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_RecoilChannel
files.Summary: One recoil output channel: baseKick + jitter per-shot, plus the solver config that drives recovery for this channel.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_RecoilController
files.Summary:
Drives camera-rotation, weapon-rotation, and weapon-position recoil for the weapon this is attached to. Writes to AFPS_WeaponObject.recoilQuaternion / .recoilPos and AFPS_Camera.recoilQuaternion — the same fields AFPS_WeaponSystem.Update() and AFPS_Camera.LateUpdate() compose into final transforms.

Maintains an independent solver triplet + pattern/momentum tracker PER profile, so a weapon with multiple fire scripts (each with its own AFPS_RecoilProfile) doesn't lose mid-decay spring state when fire modes switch. ApplyToHost sums every cached profile's current outputs each frame.

On a weapon swap, the outgoing controller keeps ticking its camera-channel springs until they decay below CamDecayEpsilonSqr — so in-flight camera recoil decays smoothly through the swap instead of snapping to zero. Weapon-mesh channels (rotation + position) reset immediately since the mesh is no longer visible. A static frame marker coordinates the shared camera field write so the decaying outgoing controller and the active incoming controller compose multiplicatively rather than race-overwriting each other.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_RecoilPatternStep
files.Summary: One row of a Scripted pattern — explicit per-shot deltas for all three channels.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_RecoilProfile
files.Summary: Authoring asset for per-weapon recoil: three independent channels (camera rotation, weapon rotation, weapon position), Procedural or Scripted pattern mode, and momentum build/cap.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_RecoilSolverConfig
files.Summary: Serializable config blob consumed by RecoilSolverFactory: solver type, spring Raw/Tuned parameters, lerp speeds, curve shape, and recovery mode/delay.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ReloadSceneRespawnStrategy
files.Summary: Restarts the level instead of respawning in it — the roguelike / "one life" answer to death. The death screen still plays in full; the reload happens when the player finally triggers the respawn.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_RespawnStrategy
files.Summary:
Where the player comes back. Swapping this asset turns a checkpoint game into an arena shooter without touching the death screen, the camera, or any code — which is the point of keeping it separate from .

Subclass and override to add your own (a spawn queue, a network handshake, a spectator hand-off).

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_ScreenEffectStatusBehaviour
files.Summary:
Status behaviour that shows a full-screen overlay on the local player while the effect is active — the "frost creeps in at the screen edges while Cold" hook. On apply it hands its to (fading the overlay in) and can fire an optional vignette pulse; on expiry it fades the overlay back out.

It only fires for the player (gated on ), so an enemy catching the same status doesn't tint the player's screen — enemies show their status in the world instead (see AFPS_StatusBehaviour subclasses for in-world VFX). No-ops gracefully when no receiver exists.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_SlotWeaponObjectSettings
files.Summary: Weapon slot assignment preset: target slot index, override/clump behaviour on slot conflict, and equip-on-pickup flags.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_SpawnOnDeath
files.Summary:
Spawns a prefab when this entity's dies, forwarding the killer (this entity's last attacker) to the spawned object so any damage it deals is credited to whoever caused the death — not to this object. The canonical use is an explosive prop: drop this next to an , point it at an explosion prefab, and a player who shoots the barrel earns the blast's damage numbers and kills, including self-inflicted chains (shoot barrel at your feet → the death reads as suicide, not "the environment").

Works for cosmetic spawns too (leave off for anonymous VFX/debris).

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_SpawnPointRegistry
files.Summary:
Scene-side list of respawn points for . The strategy is a ScriptableObject and so cannot hold scene references — this component is where the actual transforms live, and the strategy asks it for one at respawn time.

Drop it on an empty GameObject and either fill by hand or parent the points under it and let gather them.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_SpawnPointRespawnStrategy
files.Summary: Respawns at one of the points registered with . Position and facing both come from the point, and the player is healed by the controller (this strategy does not restore HP itself), so it drops straight into arena-style games with no checkpoint anywhere.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_SpreadPellet
files.Summary: One authored pellet for a Fixed pattern — a normalized offset within the spread disc.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_SpreadProfile
files.Summary: Authoring asset for per-weapon bullet spread. Defines a spread cone (maxSpreadAngle) plus how individual pellets are placed inside it: Random (uniform / gaussian / ring distribution) or Fixed (hand-authored deterministic pellet layout). Fire scripts call ApplySpread() per pellet; there is no runtime state — spread is computed fresh each shot.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_SprintMovementSettings
files.Summary: Sprint preset: toggle/hold mode, omni-directional flag, and separate ground/air drag, acceleration, and max-speed values for sprinting.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StaminaMovementSettings
files.Summary: Stamina preset: max pool, deplete/regain rates, post-exhaust sprint lockout duration, and infinite-stamina override toggle.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatsADSSettings
files.Summary: ADS preset: sensitivity/speed multipliers, spread scalar, LeanTween-driven position/rotation/FOV/crosshair/scope transition timings and easing types.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatsProjectileFireSettings
files.Summary: Projectile-fire preset: launch force/torque, fire position/direction, velocity offsets, fire delay, inventory-driven ammo/magazine settings, and UI impulse.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatsProjectileSettings
files.Summary: In-flight projectile preset: custom gravity, bounce layers/count/velocity multiplier, pierce, damage type, destroy-on-hit flags, and optional timed self-destruct.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatsRaycastFireSettings
files.Summary: Raycast-fire preset: distance, fire position/direction, spread/shot count, pierce (PhysicsMaterial dictionary), bounce, damage falloff curve, ammo/magazine, and UI impulse.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatsWeaponObjectSettings
files.Summary: Weapon fire-mode preset: primary/secondary switch cooldowns, simultaneous-fire lockout timers, and sprint/sprint-tilt interrupt durations per fire mode.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatusBehaviour
files.Summary:
Base ScriptableObject for a non-HP side effect of a status (slow, freeze, VFX, …). An lists any number of these; drives their lifecycle: once when the effect is added, on every reapply tick, and once when it ends (by timeout, chain, or being cleared on respawn — so anything applied in is always undone).

Behaviours are shared, stateless config (one asset drives many targets); keep per-target state on the target, keyed by . See for a worked example.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatusContext
files.Summary: Snapshot of who a status behaviour is acting on, passed to every lifecycle hook on . Carries the target's and the specific runtime instance — behaviours use as a per-effect key so each stack registers and cleans up its own state (e.g. one slow multiplier per Cold stack).

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatusEffect
files.Summary: ScriptableObject template for a status effect: defines build-up threshold, tick rate, HP/overheal delta, damage type, stack cap, non-HP behaviours, and an optional chained effect. At runtime instantiates a from this template.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatusOtherEffect
files.Summary: Base for non-HP side effects paired with a tick (e.g. slow, freeze, knockback). Override to implement behavior.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatusScreenEffects
files.Summary:
Player-side receiver that renders full-screen status overlays (frost, fire, poison haze) and, optionally, fires the camera's vignette. It is a singleton — the local player owns the one instance — so status behaviours can reach it from anywhere via without a scene reference.

Setup (one receiver per scene, on the local player's HUD): add this component to a Screen Space - Overlay Canvas — or to any child of one — or leave it anywhere and assign a Canvas to . drives it. Overlays are keyed by the applying effect instance, so each active effect gets its own layer and cleans up independently.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatusVFXAnchor
files.Summary: Marks a point on a character where status VFX can attach, and authors how the VFX sits there. Place these on bones or empties (chest, head, hands) and give each an ; an whose anchor id matches spawns its VFX at this transform, applying the and below as WORLD values (not multiplied by this bone's own rotation/scale), so the VFX reads the same wherever the bone happens to be pointed or scaled. Several anchors may share an id to place the same effect at multiple points (e.g. fire on both hands), each with its own rotation and scale. Optional — an enemy with no anchors just gets the VFX at its root.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatusVFXBinder.VFXOverride
files.Summary: One per-enemy override: which status effect it targets, the prefab to use, and an optional anchor override.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatusVFXBinder
files.Summary: Optional per-enemy override map for status VFX. Place it on an enemy to give specific status effects a different look than their behaviour's default — a fire elemental burning brighter than a soldier, or a boss whose frost coats a custom mesh. Status effects not listed here fall back to the VFX authored on their , so this is purely additive.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StatusVFXRegistry
files.Summary: Per-target bookkeeping for status VFX spawned by . Behaviours are shared, stateless assets and can't hold the instances they spawn, so the spawned objects are tracked here — on the target itself, keyed by the effect instance — and torn down when the effect ends or the target is destroyed. Added automatically at runtime; not meant to be placed by hand.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_StoredContents
files.Summary: World-side carrier of nested storage. Written by Drop before UI ItemObject is destroyed; read by Pickup after the new one is created.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Team
files.Summary: Identity card for a team: name, color, friendly-fire flags, and allied-team list queried by AFPS_Agent alliance checks.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Trigger
files.Summary: Unity trigger volume that routes OnTriggerEnter/Exit to UnityEvents based on TriggerType (any collision, any agent, or player-only).

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_UIImpulse
files.Summary: Scales this RectTransform on TriggerImpulse: gain → hold → decay via LeanTween, cancelling any in-flight sequence on re-fire.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_UIManager
files.Summary: Central HUD coordinator: fans weapon/ammo/health/crosshair/impulse/compass/interaction data to registered IHUDLayer implementations (UGUI + UI Toolkit).

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_UISway
files.Summary: Offsets this RectTransform's anchoredPosition each LateUpdate by lerped camera-input sway + rigidbody-velocity sway.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_UIToolkitSway
files.Summary: UI Toolkit port of AFPS_UISway. Drives style.translate on the named VisualElement in lieu of RectTransform.anchoredPosition. Attach beside the UIDocument.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_VFXStatusBehaviour
files.Summary:
Status behaviour that shows an in-world VFX on the target while the effect is active — fire on a burning enemy, frost on a chilled one. It spawns a prefab when the effect starts and destroys it when the effect ends.

Two simple pieces make it up: this behaviour (drop it on the status effect, set the prefab and which anchor to attach to) and markers you place on bones, each authoring WHERE the VFX sits plus its world rotation and scale there. If an enemy has no matching anchor, the VFX attaches to the target root — so it works on any target, authored or not. For a per-enemy look (a different prefab on a specific enemy) add an to that enemy; otherwise this default is used everywhere.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_VerticalMovementSettings
files.Summary: Jump/gravity preset: coyote time, multi-jump count, ground/air jump forces, hold-to-jump setting, horizontal velocity change on air-jump, and stamina cost.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_VignetteFlash
files.Summary: Data preset for a timed vignette flash: color, intensity, and fade-in / hold / fade-out durations.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_WallInteractionMovementSettings
files.Summary: Wall-interaction preset: detection layers/distances, walljump side/up forces, max-touch count per wall, and wallrun gravity/force overrides.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_Weapon
files.Summary: Identity card for a weapon type: HUD display name, category label, icon sprite, and linked AFPS_Item.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_WeaponAmmo
files.Summary: One ammo pool per weapon. In Magazine mode the loaded mag is an AFPS_ItemObject inside the weapon's storedItems; bullets are stacked AFPS_ItemObjects inside that mag's storedItems (LIFO fire order, mixed ammo allowed).

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_WeaponAnimSlot
files.Summary: The clip slots the weapon animator template exposes. The enum order IS the slot order used by and every other per-slot array in the runtime and editor, so the tables stay index-aligned without a dictionary lookup in Awake. Append new slots at the END only — inserting one would silently re-map cached slot indices.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_WeaponAnimationEventReceiver
files.Summary:
Forwards Unity AnimationEvents from a weapon clip to sounds and UnityEvents, keyed by string, so mag drops, shell ejects and bolt clicks need no code.

Must live on the SAME GameObject as the Animator: Unity dispatches animation events to components on the animated object itself, not on its parents.

HARD RULE: everything reachable from here is cosmetic. Animation events must never drive ammo, damage, or weapon state — gameplay timing is owned by AFPS_WeaponObject and AFPS_WeaponAmmo, and a clip that gets retimed, interrupted or speed-synced would otherwise desync real game state.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_WeaponAnimator
files.Summary:
Drives a weapon's Mecanim Animator from the gameplay events the existing weapon systems already raise (fire emitted, reload started/ended, equip/de-equip started), so authored clips play on the rig BELOW the weapon root while bob, sway, tilt, recoil, bump and ADS keep composing the root itself in .

Everything here is optional and additive. With no Animator, no override controller, or an empty clip slot, the matching procedural behaviour (LeanTween equip tween, reload tilt stance) runs exactly as it did before this component existed — a weapon that never gets one is untouched.

Gameplay stays authoritative: clips adapt their playback SPEED to the fire rate and , never the other way round. Animation events are cosmetic only (see ).

Lives on the weapon ROOT beside ; the Animator itself must live on or under the weaponModel child, because the root's localPosition/localRotation is rewritten every frame by AFPS_WeaponSystem and an Animator there would fight it.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_WeaponAnimatorContract
files.Summary:
Single source of truth for the weapon animator template's state names, parameter names, and their pre-hashed IDs. Users extending the template keep the runtime working by keeping these names — nothing else in the system contains an animator string literal, so editing this file and regenerating the template is the only change needed to alter the contract.

Every hash is a static readonly computed from a const string: a pure computation with no mutable static state, so it survives Enter Play Mode with domain reload disabled.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_WeaponBob
files.Summary: Velocity-scaled sine-wave weapon bob: writes bobPos/bobQuaternion to AFPS_WeaponObject each frame, with idle/grounded/sliding state gates.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_WeaponBump
files.Summary: Weapon bump: a camera-forward raycast engages a pos/rot offset (bumpPositionChange/bumpRotationChange) while wall-touching, reconciled toward engaged/cleared every frame so it can't strand offset; also gates canFire while wall-touching.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_WeaponObject
files.Summary: Core weapon component: manages fire-type pipeline (Automatic/Burst/Single/Charge/OnPressAndRelease), equip/drop/inventory wiring, transform offset composition, and input subscription lifecycle.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_WeaponSway
files.Summary: Camera-input-driven weapon sway: lerps/slerps/smoothdamps rotation and position offsets into AFPS_WeaponObject.swayQuaternion/swayPos.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_WeaponSystem
files.Summary: Slot-based weapon manager: equip/unequip, switch (number key/cycle/scroll/last), compose transform offsets from all weapon sub-systems, and sync HUD icons each frame.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_WeaponTilt
files.Summary: State-machine-driven weapon tilt: resolves the stance from AFPS_WeaponObject.movement.currentMovementState each frame and continuously blends pos/rot toward it. No one-shot tweens or lockouts, so the offset can never be stranded.

files.Title: AFPS.AFPS_WeaponTiltSettings
files.Summary: Maps each MovementState to a WeaponTiltStanceSetting; drives AFPS_WeaponTilt position/rotation transitions.

files.Title: AFPS.AbilityBase
files.Summary:
Base for all abilities. Subclass and override for press/release abilities or for charge abilities.

Lifecycle: at runtime the prefab is either pre-placed on the player (legacy / inspector loadout path) or instantiated by as a child of the system when the player equips a matching pickup. Either way, Awake binds to the player references on the host GameObject — so the script MUST live on, or under, a GameObject that carries AFPS_Movement / AFPS_PlayerSoundManager.

Trigger-defaults: the fields in the "Trigger Defaults" group below are the per-prefab authored defaults that the pickup-driven equip path copies into the runtime . They have no effect for inspector-pre-equipped holders (those carry their own copy of the same fields on AbilityHolder itself).

files.Title: AFPS.AbilityFire
files.Summary:
Bridges the ability system into the weapon system: a fire script that activates an instead of emitting a shot, so any ability can be the way a weapon fires. Drop it into a weapon's primary or secondary fire scripts and the weapon's existing pipeline — fire type, fire rate, burst, recoil profile, sprint interrupt, equip/drop — drives the ability.

Trigger timing belongs entirely to the weapon. The ability's own and are ignored here — those drive the slot path, and honouring both would put two invisible cooldowns on one trigger. The ability keeps ownership of validity through , which gates the recoil kick.

Press/release map straight across, because Fire(released) and ActivateAbility(pressed) are inverses of each other: pair a held ability such as with the OnPressAndRelease fire type and set , and press-to-grapple / release-to-let-go works with no ability-specific code.

files.Title: AFPS.AbilityHolder
files.Summary: Runtime state for a single equipped ability slot: holds the live AbilityBase instance, trigger configuration, cooldown timer, and burst/charge bookkeeping.

files.Title: AFPS.AbilitySource
files.Summary: Where an gets its ability from: a component authored on the weapon prefab, or a prefab it spawns and owns.

files.Title: AFPS.AmmoStorageMode
files.Summary: Determines how ammo is tracked: Simple (direct int), Loose (inventory item count), Magazine (physical mag item in storedItems), or Infinite.

files.Title: AFPS.ArmAnimation
files.Summary: One arm animation clip: velocity-speed scaling flag, repeat toggle, and the AnimationClip to play.

files.Title: AFPS.Consume
files.Summary:
Spends one unit of the item and applies its effects to the player: healing, overheal, damage, and any number of status effects. Covers medkits, bandages, food, stimulants, drugs with a downside, and poison — all from the same button prefab, configured per item menu.

The item is only spent when something actually happened, so a full-health player clicking a medkit doesn't waste it (turn off if you'd rather they could).

Effects are applied through 's normal paths, so damage numbers, the health HUD, resistances and kill attribution all behave exactly as they do for world damage.

files.Title: AFPS.ContainerLootTiming
files.Summary: When a container's loot table is rolled.

files.Title: AFPS.Crosshair
files.Summary: Per-state crosshair definition: sprite, size/rotation/color, LeanTween transition timings, and velocity-driven scale parameters.

files.Title: AFPS.CrouchHoldSetting
files.Summary: Whether crouching activates on press (toggle) or requires hold.

files.Title: AFPS.CurveRecoilSolver
files.Summary: Plays the configured AnimationCurve scaled by the most recent kick magnitude. Best for hand-authored, predictable patterns.

files.Title: AFPS.DamageInfo
files.Summary: Payload passed to : positive amount = damage, negative = healing; carries type, instigator, and optional hit geometry. is an asset (null = untyped). A value type passed by copy, and relays such as and deliberately mutate their local copy (scaling amount, tagging the hit) before forwarding it.

files.Title: AFPS.DamageNumberEvent
files.Summary: Fired by after resistances resolve. Carries the actual post-resistance magnitude (always positive) plus the data a floating-number renderer needs; UI systems resolve crit/heal styling from and , and can tint by 's colour.

files.Title: AFPS.DamageType
files.Summary: Classifies incoming damage for resistance lookups, status-effect sourcing, and analytics.

files.Title: AFPS.DamageTypeResistance
files.Summary: Maps an to a damage multiplier; values below 1 reduce damage, above 1 increase it, negative values convert damage to healing.

files.Title: AFPS.Dash
files.Summary:
Impulse dash with three direction modes, an optional charge-up windup, and a momentum window that decides how much of the dash the player keeps.

The dash fires a single along one of three directions — the camera's aim, the player's movement input, or straight up (see ) — scaled by a ground or air force. The two modes that can launch the player off the ground suppress 's hover float for a moment, because the float PID holds a fixed hover height and would otherwise push back against the launch.

Momentum preservation is a drag window rather than a force: the controller's ground and air acceleration only ever add speed along the movement vector, so nothing brakes a dash except , which rewrites from its own state every frame. For seconds after a dash this script re-applies a scaled-down damping on every physics step — reading the controller's authored value through rather than the body's own, so several physics steps inside one frame can't compound the reduction. The window ends early when the player lands, jumps, slides, or steers hard against the dash, so it never fights the action the player just chose.

The optional charge-up bleeds speed off in place for a windup and then fires automatically, hanging the player in the air (gravity and float cancelled) and locking movement input for the duration if the preset asks for it. Aim stays free throughout, and the dash direction is sampled when the impulse actually fires, so the player can steer a charged dash with the mouse.

The windup is the ability's own, and is independent of the holder's trigger type: pairing it with a Charge-type holder gives the player a held charge followed by this windup, and the holder's trigger rate starts counting from the press rather than from the moment the impulse lands.

Every tuning value lives on an preset, so the whole feel of the dash swaps with one asset. Only the per-instance SFX containers stay on the component.

files.Title: AFPS.DashMode
files.Summary:
Which direction a impulse is fired along.

keeps the dash on the movement plane and is the classic ground-dash; the other two deliberately throw the player off the ground, which is why they suppress the hover float for — the PID would otherwise fight the launch and flatten it.

files.Title: AFPS.DashVelocityReset
files.Summary: Which components of the player's velocity clears, so a dash can wipe the slate without also throwing away a jump arc.

files.Title: AFPS.DeathBodyMode
files.Summary: What the player's body does while they are dead.

files.Title: AFPS.DeathCameraPose
files.Summary: A camera pose sampled by an : where the camera is, where it looks, and how wide.

files.Title: AFPS.DeathContainerPlacement
files.Summary: Where the container holding a dropped inventory ends up.

files.Title: AFPS.DeathContext
files.Summary:
Everything the death flow knows about one death, built once by and handed to every subsystem that participates: camera modes, the death screen, respawn strategies, and user code listening on the controller's events.

This is a class rather than a struct on purpose — camera modes read it every LateUpdate, and the body handler writes back into it after spawning a corpse.

files.Title: AFPS.DeathPhase
files.Summary: Where a death sequence currently is.

files.Title: AFPS.Destroy
files.Summary: Removes the item from the inventory grid (clearing cell refs) and destroys its GO.

files.Title: AFPS.DoubleClickBehaviour
files.Summary: Scope of the stack-consolidation sweep triggered by double-click on a held item.

files.Title: AFPS.DragableRotationMode
files.Summary: Controls how the rotation PID target is resolved while a is held.

files.Title: AFPS.Drop
files.Summary:
Drops the item into the world and destroys its UI object.

Routes through . This gives it a home that doesn't depend on what's selected.

files.Title: AFPS.EditorTools.AFPS_ADSPreviewSession
files.Summary:
Drives the edit-mode ADS preview: stages a throwaway copy of a weapon under the scene's AFPS_WeaponSystem, poses it through , and drives the real main/weapon camera FOVs — which makes the GAME VIEW a true ADS render (the same two-camera composite as play mode, rather than a simulation of it).

Nothing authored is mutated. The staged weapon is a plain clone flagged HideFlags.DontSave, so it can never be serialized into a scene or applied back to a prefab. The camera FOVs are the only writes to real components; they're cached and restored on every teardown path, and temporarily reverted around a scene save so a save taken mid-preview can't bake the aimed FOV.

The preview stops (rather than trying to survive) on domain reload, play mode, scene change and editor quit — cheaper to re-toggle than to make cross-reload state correct.

files.Title: AFPS.EditorTools.AFPS_ADSValidation
files.Summary:
Checks the structural assumptions the ADS aimed pose is built on. None of these produce an error at runtime — they all just make the sight quietly fail to land where the designer expects, which is the whole reason they're worth surfacing in the inspector.

The aimed pose collapses to weapon.localPosition = -adsPoint.localPosition with identity rotation, which parks the aim point exactly on the weapon system's origin. Everything below is a precondition of that identity holding.

Split into weapon-level and rig-level checks: a weapon prefab on its own can be checked for the first set, but the rig set needs a scene with a player in it.

files.Title: AFPS.EditorTools.AFPS_ADSValidationWindow
files.Summary:
Project-wide ADS setup audit. The per-weapon inspector only tells you about the weapon you happen to be looking at; this catches the weapons nobody re-checked after a rig change — which is the way these break in practice, since none of them produce a runtime error.

Deliberately NOT an alignment report: the aimed sight position is fixed by the hierarchy (the aim point is parked on the weapon system's origin), so there is no per-weapon offset to measure. What varies, and what this checks, is whether each weapon still satisfies the structural preconditions that identity depends on.

files.Title: AFPS.GrapplingHook
files.Summary:
High-velocity, momentum-driven grapple

On press a ray sets a fixed world-space anchor. While held, the Rigidbody is reeled toward the anchor with an eased "windup" pull that ramps to full force, and is constrained to an inextensible, ratcheting rope so it swings as a pendulum; movement input adds perpendicular swing force for player-driven arcs. The rope conserves and compounds kinetic energy, so releasing slingshots the player forward with the accumulated momentum.

Anchors may be movable: hooking a non-kinematic reels both ends toward each other and splits the rope between them by mass, so a crate flies to the player while a boulder pulls the player instead. See for the split and for how each rope term is shared. Static geometry, kinematic bodies and anything past the mass ceiling behave exactly as before, and the rope end tracks a moving anchor so the LineRenderer stays glued to it.

Auto-detaches when the player crouches, is reeled all the way to the anchor (slingshotting past it), looks too far away from the anchor, drives face-on into a solid obstacle, loses line of sight along the rope for long enough that it would be running through a wall, or the anchor body is destroyed mid-swing. The grapple is released by letting go of the button

All physics is applied through forces — the transform is never moved directly — and both Update and FixedUpdate are written to avoid managed allocations (no Debug.Log, no allocating physics queries, struct-only math).

Every tuning value lives on an preset, so the whole feel of the grapple swaps with one asset. Only the per-instance references — the rope LineRenderer and the SFX containers — stay on the component.
